data.name: Thurston
data.long_meaning: Thurstan or Thurstanus is derived from the Old English words thor, meaning thunder, and stan, meaning stone. This name was given to strong, fierce protectors in ancient England. In the Anglo-Saxon culture, names often reflected a person's occupation or status, and Thurstan was a name for a warrior or a nobleman.

data.cultural_impact: Thurstan was a name synonymous with courage and strength in Anglo-Saxon England. It was a name given to protectors and warriors, symbolizing their powerful connection with the elemental force of thunder. Thurstan men were esteemed for their bravery and leadership, often assuming positions of power and authority in their communities.

Additionally, the name reminds us of the power and protection that can only come from a connection to the divine.
